title: embed-rank-pagination-tombstone-and-retry-hint-playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Legacy clients and third-party vector stores expect different pagination idioms and error signals from our embeddings and rerank endpoints. This ticket defines a compatibility playbook that harmonizes pagination tokens, handles tombstoned/deleted items without breaking cursors, and standardizes retry/error hints (Retry-After, backoff headers) across embed and rerank APIs.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic pagination contract is published that supports both cursor tokens in response bodies and Link headers for legacy clients.
Deleted/tombstoned results do not cause page shifts for stable cursors; downstream clients can detect tombstones via a stable 'status' field on results.
HTTP error mapping documented: 400->client error for invalid cursor, 422->malformed payload, 429 with Retry-After for rate limits, 503 with X-Redwood-Retry for transient capacity issues.
Embed and rerank endpoints use the same cursor encoding and forward-compatible semantic version key so clients can detect incompatible cursor formats.
Backwards-compatible adapter layer implemented that responds with both next_cursor and Link headers for 6 months behind a feature flag.
Integration tests exist that validate order stability, consistent page sizes, and cursor immutability across small model rollouts.
Observability: per-cursor metrics (pages served, tombstones encountered, invalid-cursor errors) are emitted to Console dashboards.
A canary rollout plan is approved and validated with three paying customers using Dedicated and Hosted tiers before global rollout.
design_notes: We propose an explicit cursor envelope: base64(JSON) with fields: v (version), p (page_size), s (server-time UUID), qh (query-hash), o (ordering-hash), t (optional tombstone-cursor-pointer). The response body will include 'results' (array) where each item has 'id', 'score', 'status' ('ok'|'tombstone'), and an optional 'deleted_at'. This lets clients detect tombstones without re-fetching pages. For legacy compatibility, include a Link header with rel="next" pointing to /v1/embeddings?page_token=... and also expose next_cursor in the JSON body. The default stable ordering is (score desc, id asc) unless a custom 'order_by' param is supplied; in that case, the cursor encodes the ordering-hash.
engineering_notes: Implementation will be an adapter in the API gateway translating legacy Link-header pagination to our canonical cursor system. Core runtime will validate cursors: invalid format -> 400, unsupported version -> 412 (Precondition Failed) with 'upgrade-suggestion' header pointing to docs. Rate limits return 429 + Retry-After seconds; transient capacity/backpressure returns 503 + X-Redwood-Retry: <ms> to suggest backoff. For rerank flows which interleave embed calls, adapter must preserve per-item stable identifiers and backfill tombstone markers when the vector store returns missing ids. Add feature flag 'compat-paging-v2' to gate dual-output behavior.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal): adapter + unit tests behind feature flag; deploy to staging; smoke tests against mock vector store
Phase 2 (canary): enable for 10% of hosted traffic and one Dedicated customer; run compatibility suite for 2 weeks
Phase 3 (partners): invite 3 external customers to opt-in to the dual-header behavior for validation
Phase 4 (global): flip default after metrics show <0.1% client errors introduced and no regression in latency; deprecate Link-only mode after a 6-month notice
test_plan: Unit tests: cursor encoding/decoding, version mismatch, corrupted tokens
Integration: end-to-end embed->rerank pagination with deliberate tombstones inserted at earlier pages to ensure downstream cursor stability
Chaos: simulate 503/backpressure and verify clients receive X-Redwood-Retry and behave per our SDK retry policies
Performance: measure 95p latency before/after adapter at target RPS and ensure <5% regression
Backward compatibility: validate Link header + next_cursor surface for legacy SDKs and a modern SDK using only next_cursor
